primary_claim: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately self-report complex, quantitative attribute weights they implicitly learned via fine-tuning (correlation r~0.5), and a second round of 'introspection training' improves this self-report accuracy to r~0.75 in held-out contexts, generalizing to attribute weights the models natively use in contexts where no preferences were instilled.

effect.metric: Pearson correlation (r) between reported and learned/used attribute weights
effect.value: r ~ 0.5 before introspection training; r ~ 0.75 after introspection training on held-out choice contexts

stated_future_work: Extending the approach to more realistic and safety-relevant domains beyond choosing between goods and services.
Developing a more varied 'introspection training' that guides models toward accurate self-report across a broader range of tasks.
Writing a follow-up post exploring the 'introspection' vs 'cached self-knowledge' mechanism distinction and possible solutions.
limitations_stated: The setup is somewhat artificial; choosing between goods and services is not the most important context for LLM decision-making.
Training generalizes only somewhat and likely doesn't yet generalize very far.
The underlying mechanism of the accurate self-reports (genuine introspection vs. cached self-knowledge) is unknown.
quote: Across choice contexts, the attribute weights that the models reported using were correlated with the attribute weights they had actually learned to use at around r = 0.5
